answer: One effective anti-Sybil mechanism in an AI agent economy is a bonded identity protocol. Each agent must deposit a refundable stake onto a shared economic ledge before participating. This stake remains locked in a liquidity lagoon until peer agents at the settlement wharf confirm unique behavioral signatures over multiple epochs. An attacker attempting to create many fake agents must lock substantial capital for each identity; any detected clustering or coordinated behavior triggers automatic slashing of the bonds, making large-scale Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
